```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "Original request and host-provided skill descriptions",
    "README.md",

    "package.json",
    "docs/api.md",

    "docs/decisions/0008-json-data-file.md",
    "scripts/weekly-report.js",
    "src/app.js",
    "src/http.js",
    "src/store.js",
    "src/tickets/query.js",
    "src/tickets/states.js",
    "src/outbox.js",
    "src/worker.js",
    "src/notifier.js",
    "src/templates.js",
    "src/persistence.js",
    "test/query.test.js",
    "test/api.test.js"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake established the ticket-service outcomes, preserved boundaries, and questions for discovery; no implementation or server run was performed.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K1"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K2"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K3"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K4"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K5"},

    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K9"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K10"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K11"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K12"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K13"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "What notification content and delivery observation make a close notice equivalent to the existing resolution heads-up?",
      "changes": "The close notification template and end-to-end acceptance check.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the resolution template, notifier and relay contract first; use a clearly worded close notice through the same outbox and notification channel, observable in notifier output.",
      "blocks": "Final notification wording and acceptance test; discovery can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, CLI, report, outbox and persistence contracts must remain unchanged while adding close notifications and bulk closing?",
      "changes": "The implementation boundary and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the API, decisions and callers first; preserve existing behavior except for the requested filter correction and new behavior, including raw report column positions and outbox retry logic.",
      "blocks": "Implementation choices that could break existing consumers."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close endpoint, body, result and error contract can support 500 ticket IDs, and how should duplicate IDs and mixed-validity requests behave?",
      "changes": "The HTTP interface, validation and bulk acceptance tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks existing routes, request limits and error conventions first; if no contract exists, use one JSON bulk request, reject duplicate IDs and validate the whole request before changing anything, returning existing error envelopes.",
      "blocks": "Final bulk API and its tests."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a recently delivered resolution notice, and how do pending, failed, dead or repeated resolution notices affect suppression of a close notice?",
      "changes": "Notification suppression rules and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks event timestamps, states and existing policy first; if no policy exists, treat a resolution notice successfully sent to the same requester for the same ticket within the preceding 24 hours as recent, and do not treat dead or failed notices as delivered.",
      "blocks": "Final suppression behavior, including the pending-notice case."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should immediate delivery and batching be reconciled, including grouping, maximum delay and notification contents?",
      "changes": "Batching design, privacy rules and timing tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks worker and relay capabilities first; enqueue on close and deliver at the next enabled worker tick, grouping eligible tickets from the same bulk operation by requester without including another requester's tickets.",
      "blocks": "Final batching and delivery contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What is the weekly-report window, including timestamp field, time zone and inclusive boundaries?",
      "changes": "The closed-ticket query and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the report, other repository documents and available workspace leads first; the inspected report counts all current tickets and establishes no window, so absent contrary evidence use the preceding seven days in UTC, inclusive at the start and exclusive at the query time, based on the final close timestamp.",
      "blocks": "Final window contract and its tests."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What query parameter selects the closed-ticket window, and how does it combine with status, priority and cursor pagination?",
      "changes": "The list API contract, validation and pagination tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks existing clients and cursor conventions first; add an explicit window selector, preserve existing defaults, combine supplied filters with AND before pagination, and retain the existing response and error envelopes.",
      "blocks": "Final parameter name, value and filter contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What state must survive restart for close times, suppression and batches, and what happens if closes or deliveries overlap?",
      "changes": "Persistence compatibility, concurrency handling and restart tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks audit and outbox history, persistence validation and worker ownership first; preserve version-1 file compatibility and single-process ownership, retain shared state until the existing data lifecycle ends it, and avoid duplicate state changes or notification effects on repeated closes.",
      "blocks": "Final state representation and concurrency guarantees."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are agents and requesters identified, what information is visible to each, and does the runtime provide authentication or sessions?",
      "changes": "Audit attribution, batch recipient isolation and security tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the HTTP and deployment boundaries first; the application records the supplied X-Actor or system and addresses notices to the ticket requester; assume no application-level authentication or session isolation and do not add either.",
      "blocks": "Any claim of verified actor identity or stronger access isolation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which runtime, configuration and body-size limits apply to a 500-ticket request and enabled notification delivery?",
      "changes": "Bulk request design and runtime verification setup.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks Node, configuration and representative request size first; use Node 22 or later, standard library only, existing configuration defaults and the existing worker controls.",
      "blocks": "A bulk contract that has not been shown to fit configured limits."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing seams can isolate bulk transitions, batching and window filtering without modifying retry logic?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and testability.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks store, query, worker, outbox and persistence seams first; keep ticket changes in the store, scheduled work in the worker and delivery through the outbox.",
      "blocks": "Implementation design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which tests and running-server observations demonstrate the requested behavior at its real boundaries, including 500 closes?",
      "changes": "The exit checks and test fixtures.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the existing node:test suite and server helpers first; require npm test plus a running-server exercise of close, notification output, suppression, batching, combined filters, audit, repeat close and a 500-ticket bulk request.",
      "blocks": "Declaring the later delivery complete; starting a server remains outside this intake."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "What delivery target and access are available, and does the repository's issue-first convention require an external issue before a PR or release?",
      "changes": "The delivery steps and any external approval or access requirement.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks repository and run context first; the named target is this checkout, with no deployment target or permission to contact others established. Prepare the result locally; an external issue or release requires the necessary authority and access.",
      "blocks": "Any external issue, PR or release whose prerequisites are unmet; local discovery and implementation can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What practical bounds demonstrate responsive bulk closing and prevent disclosure in batched notices?",
      "changes": "Bulk and recipient-isolation acceptance checks.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "After discovery checks existing limits and relay behavior, require a 500-ticket bulk call to complete successfully without a user-specified numerical latency target, and never combine different requesters' ticket details in one message.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can immediate enqueueing, recipient batching, restart safety and unchanged retry behavior coexist with the existing relay and worker contracts?",
      "changes": "The design and earliest integration checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks relay keys, worker scheduling and outbox persistence first; retain existing retry behavior and test delivery and restart boundaries before claiming the design works.",
      "blocks": "Final batching design and completion claim."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q16",
      "category": "K13",
      "question": "How should repeated close requests reconcile idempotence with a 409 response?",
      "changes": "Repeat-close response and side-effect tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the existing transition contract first; retain 409 conflict for an already closed ticket while making the repeated request effect-idempotent: no new change, audit entry or notification.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded default proceeds unless discovery finds a conflicting contract."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q17",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "How should until-loop, backchain and optional ralph-style execution be applied in the later run, and what cap is appropriate?",
      "changes": "The later run's sequencing, continuation condition and stop limit.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery checks the host's installed skill instructions first; backchain before implementation, continue an evidence-driven loop until both requested exit checks pass or a real blocker arises, and do not start an overnight loop; if one is later chosen, cap it at 10 iterations or 8 hours, whichever comes first.",
      "blocks": "Later orchestration details; intake and repository discovery can proceed."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact] The target is the help desk ticket service in this checkout; S2 [outcome, open Q1/Q4] notify the requester on close and suppress a redundant recent resolution notice; S3 [outcome, open Q5] enqueue promptly and batch bulk-close notices without cross-recipient disclosure; S4 [outcome, open Q6/Q7] expose closed tickets from the established reporting window through the list API; S5 [fact/outcome] supplied filters must intersect as documented; S6 [fact] inspection found the current matcher uses OR, contrary to the documented AND, so later work must correct and verify it; S7 [boundary, open Q12/Q17] backchain before implementation and use an evidence-driven loop whose exit requires green tests and a working running-server exercise; S8 [default Q17] overnight execution is optional and, if used, capped at 10 iterations or 8 hours; S9 [outcome] verify behavior with meaningful boundary tests and keep documentation accurate and concise; S10 [boundary] leave outbox retry logic untouched, with OldTracker migration only the stated rationale; S11 [boundary] use Node's standard library without added dependencies; S12 [default Q16] repeated close returns 409 without another state change, audit entry or notification, while the original close records the supplied actor; S13 [outcome, open Q3/Q10/Q14] one bulk call must successfully close 500 eligible tickets with responsive operation but no invented latency target. [Facts] The report inspected counts all current tickets and does not establish a time window; no bulk endpoint was found in the current routes; the existing worker delivers asynchronously and can be disabled; X-Actor is caller-supplied and defaults to system; the service keeps shared ticket, audit and outbox state in memory or one optional data file, with one process owning that file. [Assumptions] There is no application-level authenticated identity, session-specific state or requester visibility boundary beyond the existing internal-network deployment; batching must isolate recipients, and no new authentication or deployment is in scope. [Discovery leads, not verified facts] Inspect the help desk team and support leads' workspace, relevant channels, internal documentation, private repositories and owners if available for the weekly window, notification policy, relay behavior and OldTracker terminology; no specific channel, site, owner or sensitive locator was supplied. [Authority and visibility] This intake reads only and starts no server; the named checkout is the delivery target, and an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return. The later outcome becomes usable in that checkout at final return and in any deployed target only after an authorized release. The repository asks for an issue before API, data-file or notification changes, but no authority to contact others is established."
}
```
